subject: GPU fallback — degraded throughput impacting Nimbus inference
content:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah@nimbus.ai>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: ops@nimbus.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: GPU fallback — degraded throughput impacting Nimbus inference

Hi Rafael,

We’re seeing a sustained period of elevated latency and an increase in model fallback events on our Dedicated pool (dpool-us-west-2-nimbus). Starting ~09:05 UTC today a subset of requests began triggering the fallback policy to a smaller model which dropped correct outputs and produced ~40% error/garbage responses for our production inference path. Impact window roughly 09:05–10:32 UTC, many customer requests timed out or returned incorrect responses.

Sample request ids: nimbus-req-8a3f, nimbus-req-8a72, nimbus-req-8b01.

Can you confirm whether this aligns with any autoscaler activity on your side or pool-level throttling? We need a short-term mitigation and an ETA for a post-incident writeup and credit discussion. This is affecting customer SLAs.

Thanks,
Sarah Liu
Head of Platform Ops
Nimbus AI

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Sarah Liu <sarah@nimbus.ai>, ops@nimbus.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 11:40:00 +0000
Subject: RE: GPU fallback — degraded throughput impacting Nimbus inference

Quick technical update from infra: we observed a sudden queue depth increase at 09:04:50 UTC across three nodes in the pool. Autoscaler attempted to scale but the new reserve nodes hit a warmup latency degenerate path (kernel selection fallback) which increased per-token time; that cascaded into our fallback heuristic triggering smaller model variants for ~27% of the in-flight requests.

Actions taken (complete):
- Drained the three affected nodes from the tenant pool and moved traffic to warm-standby nodes (warm standby handled ~80% of diverted traffic).
- Applied a temporary autoscaler override to cap parallel slot churn and prefer existing warm nodes over instant provisioning.
- Forced a consistent kernel selection profile on the warm standby nodes (reverted to verified conservative kernels).

Immediate mitigation commands we ran are included in attached mitigation_commands.txt (short command list). Estimated customer-visible recovery: verified drop in fallback events by 10:28 UTC; full throughput returned by 10:45 UTC for most request classes.

We’re collecting the low-level telemetry and creating an event timeline (attached as timeline.csv) and a correlation graphic (initial_event_correlation.png).

Ben Carter
Infrastructure Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com

Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2028 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: GPU fallback — degraded throughput impacting Nimbus inference

Sarah — thank you and apologies again for the customer impact. Summary and next steps below.

Summary (brief):
- Root cause: an autoscaler/warmup interaction where newly provisioned nodes briefly selected a slower kernel path under the observed request-length distribution; that increased token-processing time and pushed autoscaler heuristics into fallback.
- Impact window: 2028-04-09 09:05–10:32 UTC (primary), residual retries through ~11:00 UTC.

Immediate remediation already applied:
- Drained affected nodes and shifted to warm standby (complete).
- Autoscaler override to prefer warm nodes + reduced slot-churn (complete).
- Conservative kernel selection enforced for warm standby for the next 72 hours.

Next steps (this week):
1) Postmortem draft: shared to the folder here — https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1NIMBUS-POSTMORTEM — draft attached as postmortem-draft.md. Please review prior to the walkthrough.
2) Credit proposal: we will calculate credit based on the measured SLO delta across 09:00–11:00 UTC; provisional offer will be in the postmortem draft.
3) Technical follow-up: engineering will run a warmup regression test and deploy a safer kernel-selection gating rule to prevent warmup-time kernel regressions (ETA 7 days).
4) Walkthrough: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 15:00–15:30 UTC — we propose 15:00 UTC for the joint session. Please confirm.

Attachments included: timeline.csv (detailed event timeline), mitigation_commands.txt (commands used during mitigation), initial_event_correlation.png (correlation graph), postmortem-draft.md (draft).

If you want the full request export for a deeper customer-side verification, we can provide a filtered log bundle (redacted) — let us know which time range and we’ll share via secure transfer.

Best regards,
Rafael Mendes
Sr. Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
